# Feature: Proxy-side proactive session compaction (Tier 1)

**STATUS: DEFERRED — implementation delayed until client-side compaction
results are available.** Client-side compaction machinery is now in place in
ContextHub (Compact-and-Continue WL-0MR269PDV00970YP, auto-continue
WL-0MSMGGPWR000MZ0O; gate-response wiring WL-0MTBOXEGR009KDP6). Per
operator decision (2026-08-28), server-side compaction must not be
implemented until results from the client-side effort are reviewed; this
item is parked (status `blocked`) pending that review.

Implementation of the F4 recommendation (LP-0MTC8BWV50012WSW,
`docs/session-compaction-recommendations.md`) within the two-tier scheme of
LP-0MTCW79RR000LFMJ. The proxy compacts the session at **prompt-assembly
time** when estimated tokens exceed the trigger — no round trip, no
client-side coordination.

## Behavior (both modes — Strategy C, summarize-first)

Per operator decision (2026-08-28), serve-side compaction uses the hybrid
Strategy C in **both** fast and cheap modes, with the **first prompt always
retained verbatim**.

### Retention invariant (fast AND cheap)

The compacted prompt MUST always contain, unchanged:

1. the system prompt;
2. the **very first user prompt** (the original task statement/setup, which
   carries essential instructions);
3. the most recent turns within budget.

Everything between the first prompt and the recent window is folded into a
summary injected at the top of the prompt (below the retained first prompt).

### Fast mode — Strategy C

- **Trigger:** `estimated_tokens > 58,300` (= 0.70 × per-slot clamp 83,285).
  Fires before the existing `context_pressure_warn_ratio` (0.8 × 83,285 =
  66.6K) so compaction is proactive, not reactive.
- **Target:** compacted prompt ≤ 38,000 tokens (`local_large_context_cold_cache_threshold`,
  fast profile): retain system prompt + first prompt + recent turns; fold
  the rest into a summary.
- **Backstop:** only if the session still exceeds budget after summarizing,
  drop oldest non-first turns (whole turns, never splittable, never the
  system prompt or first prompt), logged.
- **Automatic** on breach.

### Cheap mode — Strategy C (hybrid)

- **Trigger:** `estimated_tokens > 43,000` (= 0.70 × static clamp 61,440).
- **Target:** compacted prompt ≤ 30,000 tokens: same retention invariant +
  summary of the middle.
- **Non-compactable** (summarizer unavailable, or still over budget after
  compaction): route remote with guidance — never silent remote fallback,
  never near-full-slot local prefill (LP-0MSORQVK50012Q4D AC4).
- **Automatic** on breach.

## Implementation approach

- **Trigger hook:** reuse the existing `context_pressure` machinery in
  `proxy/provider.py` (`context_pressure_ratio` / `should_warn_context_pressure`,
  LP-0MSDCLQ2W001LGWC). Add a configurable compaction trigger ratio
  (default 0.70), distinct from the 0.8 diagnostic warn ratio (unchanged).
- **Compaction at prompt assembly:** session history is a message list;
  summarization/truncation operates on it before dispatch. Composes with
  slot save/restore (compacted prompts restore cleanly under the
  persistence cap).
- **Summarizer:** short proxy-generated summary (cheap local call) injected
  at the top of the prompt; with summarizer-unavailable fallback to the
  truncate backstop.
- **Logging:** every compaction event logs session, before/after estimated
  tokens, turns summarized, turns dropped, summary length — traceability
  for quality regressions (F3 §7). Nothing is silent.
- **Rollout phases:**
  1. **Warn-only dry-run** — advisory (would-summarize/would-drop) log +
     stats for 48h; validate churn (< 1 compaction/session/hour) against
     F1/F2 distributions; **no dispatch behavior change**.
  2. **Enforcement** — gated on the quality experiment (LP-0MSG9PUHU0059TTZ)
     passing its bar AND operator review of client-side compaction results.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1 Both modes: compacted prompt retains system prompt + very first user
  prompt verbatim + recent turns; middleware summarized (never silently
  dropped).
- AC2 Fast: est > 58,300 → compacted to ≤ 38K; backstop drop only for
  non-summarizable middle turns, logged, never system/first prompt.
- AC3 Cheap: est > 43,000 → compacted to ≤ 30K; non-compactable → remote
  with guidance (never silent remote, never near-full-slot local dispatch).
- AC4 Trigger routed through `context_pressure` machinery; compaction
  trigger ratio 0.70 configurable; 0.8 warn ratio behavior unchanged.
- AC5 All compaction events logged (session, before/after est tokens, turns
  summarized, turns dropped, summary length).
- AC6 Warn-only dry-run phase produces advisory logs + churn stats with
  zero dispatch changes; dry-run threshold validation recorded.
- AC7 Unit tests: retention invariant (first prompt kept), summary path,
  truncate backstop boundaries, turn-split prohibition, non-compactable
  routing, warn-only mode. Full suite green.
- AC8 Enforcement only after experiment (LP-0MSG9PUHU0059TTZ) passes its
  bar AND client-side compaction review (ContextHub WL-0MTBOXEGR009KDP6) is
  complete; no behavior change in warn-only phase.

## Interaction analysis (from F4 §5)

- **Slot save/restore:** summary + recent turns are byte-stable → clean
  restores under the persistence cap.
- **Hard-routing-cap companion (Tier 2, LP-0MTBOX45O005LD1S):** cap at
  70K/61.4K is the final bypass guard; compaction trigger fires below it so
  sessions rarely reach the cap.
- **KV-cache quantization (LP-0MSDCLQ2W001LGWC):** additive — compaction
  shrinks context length, q8_0 shrinks bytes/token; both raise decode
  headroom.

## Out of scope

- Client-side compaction UX (ContextHub owns it; see WL-0MTBOXEGR009KDP6).
- 150K–480K HTTP-400 cluster (LP-0MSC1BNP90017L9K).
- Changing the 0.8 diagnostic warn ratio.

## Dependencies

- Depends on LP-0MSG9PUHU0059TTZ (quality experiment) for the enforcement
  go/no-go.
- **Blocked pending:** client-side compaction results (ContextHub
  WL-0MTBOXEGR009KDP6 and completed compact-and-continue machinery) —
  operator decision 2026-08-28 to delay server-side until those are
  reviewed.
- Complementary to LP-0MTBOX45O005LD1S (Tier 2 hard cap + cheap gate).
data.title: Implement proxy-side proactive session compaction (Tier 1: truncate 58.3K / hybrid 43K)

discovered-from:LP-0MTZRM5HV0007S0V

The slot_schedule removal (LP-0MTZRM5HV0007S0V) removes the time-based slot schedule from proxy/config.yaml, config-fast.yaml, config-cheap.yaml.

The proxy-usage-analysis skill (.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/) still parses slot_schedule from the active config to derive per-time slot counts and ctx: scripts/config_loader.py (_normalize), scripts/bucketing.py (schedule_from_config), scripts/reporting.py (ctx_by_time), scripts/recommendations.py (advice pointing at 'proxy/config.yaml slot_schedule').

Impact: with no slot_schedule key, config_loader omits it and bucketing falls back to a single 'fast' bucket with default_slots (session_slot_pool_size) for the whole day — the cheap (2-slot) vs fast (3-slot) slot-count split is lost.

Required work (in the skill directory, per .pi boundary this item must be explicitly authorized):
- Derive per-mode slot counts from the mode profiles' static session_slot_pool_size (fast 3 / cheap 2) instead of schedule entries.
- Replace ctx_by_time semantics with the profiles' static local_model_ctx_size.
- Update recommendations text that references 'proxy/config.yaml slot_schedule'.
- Update skill tests/fixtures accordingly.
data.title: proxy-usage-analysis: drop slot_schedule dependency after per-mode slot-count simplification
Increase summarizer_max_tokens to 1024 and add client compaction-sync validation

## Problem statement

The refactor skill filed an `E741` ("ambiguous variable name: `l`") finding at
line 4756 of `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py`
and injected a `REFACTOR-LP-0MVDFQC2X005S7WE` marker. Investigation shows the
finding is a **false positive**: no committed revision of the file has ever
contained an `l` identifier, and `ruff check` on the current file passes.

## Users

- **Maintainers of the proxy-usage-analysis skill** — need a worklog that does
  not carry phantom technical debt.
- **The refactor skill / future lint sweeps** — need accurate detection; stale
  markers suppress future findings for the same smell type in this file.

User stories:

- As a maintainer, I want the worklog to reflect real defects so triage time is
  not spent re-verifying already-clean code.
- As an agent running `/skill:refactor`, I want a stale `REFACTOR` marker to be
  removed once its smell no longer exists, so the marker does not mask new
  findings.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `ruff check --select E741 .pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py` reports no findings.
- [ ] An AST scan (or equivalent) confirms no `Name`/`arg` identifier equal to `l` (or the other E741 names `O`/`I`) exists in the file.
- [ ] The work item's disposition is recorded in a comment: either **closed as resolved-in-parent** (smell fixed before parent commit `c0f3625f`, no code change) or the stale `REFACTOR-LP-0MVDFQC2X005S7WE` marker block is removed from the file.
- [ ] Testing/validation criterion: the verification commands above are documented in the work item so a reviewer can reproduce the conclusion.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The finding references a **deleted worktree path**
  (`.worklog/worktrees/wl-LP-0MVC144KS001PDR4-surface-attribution-in-reporting-py/`);
  the authoritative file is the main checkout copy.
- `AGENTS.md` repository boundaries: `.pi/` must not be edited unless
  explicitly instructed — removing the marker requires explicit authorisation.
- The repo already carries other stale `REFACTOR` markers (e.g.
  `LP-0MTHLGVPO004DZ56` in the same file, `LP-0MTGDB3D9007TWHA`,
  `LP-0MVB0THT7000KT0G`); a one-off removal would be inconsistent without the
  systemic fix.

## Existing state

- Current HEAD file: 5,023 lines; line 4756 is the docstring
  `"""LP-0MVC144KS001PDR4 — attribution surfaces in the report."""` — a docstring,
  not a variable.
- Every committed revision (40 commits touching the file) checked: zero
  standalone `l` identifiers. `git log -S "for l in"` returns nothing.
- `ruff check` on the file: **All checks passed!**
- AST scan for `Name`/`arg` in `{l, O, I}`: **NONE**.
- The parent item `LP-0MVC144KS001PDR4` ("Surface attribution in reporting.py")
  is `completed`/`done`; its commit `c0f3625f` is the one that both injected the
  marker and (evidently) landed the fixed file — so the smell was resolved in
  the same session, before commit.

## Desired change

Minimal: record the false-positive/resolved-in-parent disposition and close the
item. Optional (requires explicit authorisation under the `.pi/` boundary
rule): delete the six-line `REFACTOR-LP-0MVDFQC2X005S7WE` marker block so the
`formatting` smell type is no longer suppressed for this file.

Systemic follow-up (out of scope, filed as `discovered-from`): the refactor
skill should remove a `REFACTOR` marker when its work item is closed — it
currently only injects (`comment_injection.py` has no removal path), so stale
markers accumulate repo-wide.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py` — lines 1–6 hold the stale `REFACTOR-LP-0MVDFQC2X005S7WE` marker block (optional removal).
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/fixtures.py` — fixtures used by the file; no change expected.
- `.ruff.toml` — confirms `E` (incl. `E741`) is selected and not ignored; no change expected.

## Related work

- `LP-0MVC144KS001PDR4` — Surface attribution in reporting.py (parent session that injected the marker; completed).
- `LP-0MTHLGVPO004DZ56` — Refactor: unused variable `schedule`, same file/marker mechanism (completed; marker still present).
- `LP-0MU1I7T37001CV4O` — ruff I001 candidate false positive at another file (closed as duplicate of an already-fixed parent finding; disposition precedent).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the `l` variable existed only in the pre-commit worktree state
  and was fixed before `c0f3625f`; the worktree is deleted, so this cannot be
  re-verified directly. Evidence: the marker was committed by the same commit
  that landed the corrected file.
- **Risk (scope creep):** "also clean up every stale REFACTOR marker" — record
  as a linked work item, not as scope here.
- **Risk:** removing the marker alone does not fix the systemic leak; without
  the systemic item, stale markers will keep accumulating.
- **Risk:** misclassifying a real finding as false positive. Mitigated by the
  reproducible AST + ruff checks in the ACs.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Is this E741 finding real, or a false positive?" — Answer (Map, evidence-based): **False positive.** No committed revision contains an `l` identifier; `ruff check` passes; AST scan finds no `l`/`O`/`I` names. Source: `git log --all -S "for l in"` (empty), `ruff check` on the file, AST walk of current HEAD, inspection of commit `c0f3625f`. Evidence path: `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py:4756`.
- Q: "Should the stale `REFACTOR` marker be removed as part of this item?" — Answer: **OPEN QUESTION for the producer.** Recommended: close as resolved-in-parent without touching `.pi/` (respects the repository-boundaries rule); file a separate `discovered-from` item for the systemic marker-removal gap. Source: agent recommendation, pending operator confirmation.

### Related work items
- **LP-0MSDFAFX0000SKQK** – Relocate proxy-usage-analysis skill from global ~/.pi/agent/skills to project-local .pi/skills (completed)
- **LP-0MSH4C63I004T4JL** – [CRITICAL] /home/rgardler/projects/llm/.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py:475 — Local variable `res` is assigned to but never used (F841) (completed)

# Goal (user story)

As a proxy operator, I want a mechanism to restrict which clients may claim high (or any non-default) request priority, so the priority-routing feature cannot be defeated by every client marking every request `X-Priority: high`.

## Background

The priority-routing epic (LP-0MVDT94F0003VHUA) ships v1 with **no trust gate** (decision d from intake): the header is honoured from any reachable client. This item tracks the hardening follow-up.

## Acceptance Criteria (draft)

- A configurable gate restricts who may request priority above `medium` (e.g. trusted-source allowlist of localhost/subnets, shared-secret header, or per-client capability map).
- Unauthorised high-priority claims are silently downgraded to `medium` (no error, no DoS by 4xx) and logged.
- Choice of gate mechanism documented in the epic's appendix; gate is off by default until operator opts in.
- All related documentation updated and full project test suite passes.
data.title: Priority header trust gate: authenticate/authorize X-Priority before trusting it (spoofing risk)

# Limiter skip log prints an impossible ratio when the reserve is in use

discovered-from:LP-0MVDUN5CY009VD20

## Problem

`SlidingWindowRateLimiter.check_and_increment()` logs the rejection ratio as
`len(window)/max_rpm`, but with the free-tier reserve
(`LP-0MVDUN5CY009VD20`) the per-caller cap can be lower than the number of
entries already in the window, producing log lines that look like a bug:

```
WARNING - Rate limit exceeded for munitoai-free: 10/7 requests in 60s window
WARNING - Provider budget exhausted: skipping provider=munitoai-free limit=7 reserve=3 ...
```

The `10` is the count in the window (including slots taken by in-progress
sessions), the `7` is the cap applied to this new-session request. Operators and
log analyses read `10/7` as an arithmetic error.

## Desired change

Make the message self-describing, e.g.:

```
Rate limit exceeded for munitoai-free: window=10 cap=7 (reserve in use) requests in 60s window
```

Keep the emitted fields parseable (stable `key=value` tokens) so the
proxy-usage / budget-effectiveness analyses can extract `window=` and `cap=`
instead of inferring them from provider config.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The rejection log line names both the in-window count and the cap applied to
  the rejected request, with no value that can read as `count/cap` confusion.
- A unit test asserts the emitted message contains `window=`, `cap=` and the
  correct numbers for (a) a plain over-limit rejection and (b) a
  reserve-limited rejection (cap < window count).
- No behaviour change: only the message text (and any consumed parse) changes;
  full project test suite passes.
- Stale references quoting the old `N/M requests in Ns window` wording are
  updated to the new format (see Affected references).

## Implementation notes

- The limiter only knows the cap it was handed (`effective_limit`); it does not
  know *why* that cap is below the configured `rate_limit_rpm`. A
  `(reserve in use)` annotation therefore requires the caller
  (`proxy/provider_budget.py`) to pass context, and is optional — the required,
  parseable fields are `window=` and `cap=`.
- If extra context is passed, prefer a stable token over prose so the
  `key=value` convention used by the companion `Provider budget exhausted`
  line is preserved (e.g. `cap=7 reserve=3`, not `(reserve in use)`).
- Test-first: add the message assertions to `proxy/tests/test_rate_limiter.py`
  (plain over-limit case and `cap < window` case) before changing the format
  string.

## Affected references

- `proxy/proxy/rate_limiter.py` — the format string and `logger.warning` call.
- `proxy/tests/test_rate_limiter.py` — unit tests asserting the message fields.
- `proxy/tests/test_chain_hold_budget_window.py` — comment quoting the old
  `13/11 requests in 60s window` wording.
- `proxy/docs/remote-fallback-timeout-budget.md` — same quoted wording.

**Key Files:**
- `proxy/proxy/rate_limiter.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_rate_limiter.py`
- `proxy/docs/remote-fallback-timeout-budget.md`
data.title: Limiter skip log prints 10/7 when the reserve is in use

# Consolidate and document the provider fallback-chain configuration model

discovered-from:LP-0MVDVK5TM004TQQV

## Goal (user story)

As the proxy operator, I want **one** authoritative description of the provider
fallback model — every knob that shapes a chain, the layer it applies at
(provider entry / model / server), and the order those layers win in — so I can
answer "how do I control X for model Y?" without reading `provider.py`, and so
new controls (e.g. per-model budget knobs, `LP-0MVDVK5TM004TQQV`) slot into a
documented contract instead of inventing a new shape.

Low priority: documentation/consolidation only, no behaviour change.

## Current state (fragmented)

Fallback behaviour is described in five places that have drifted apart:
`proxy/config.yaml` header comments, `proxy/README.md`, `proxy/MODEL_ADD.md`,
`proxy/docs/routing.md` and inline code comments in `proxy/proxy/provider.py` /
`provider_budget.py`. The knobs themselves are spread across three layers with
no single statement of precedence:

| Layer | Examples | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Provider entry | `rate_limit_rpm`, `available_times`, `endpoint`, `api_key_env`, `forward_session_headers`, `api`, `system_prompt`, `budget` (proposed) | per-entry, order defines chain position |
| Model (`models.<name>`) | `providers` list order, `aliases`, `system_prompt`, `budget` (proposed) | one model key → one chain, shared by all aliases |
| Server (`server.*`) | `provider_cooldown_seconds`, `sibling_fallback_*`, `chain_hold_*`, `upstream_*`, `provider_rate_limit_*`, `provider_affinity_ttl_seconds`, `max_retry_after_seconds` | global; some are inherited-only across mode overlays |
| Mode overlay | `config-fast.yaml`, `config-cheap.yaml` | lists replace wholesale; other values replace; only diffs declared |
| Runtime | cooldowns, usage-limit quarantine, stall circuit breaker, affinity records, budget windows | in-memory + `proxy/provider-state.json` |

Cross-cutting semantics that are easy to get wrong and belong in one place:
failure-domain grouping (shared endpoint+model), per-account vs per-endpoint
exclusion, time windows (`available_times`), the free-tier budget gate
(`LP-0MVDQ1GMO00801PL`, `LP-0MVDUN5CY009VD20`) including the reserve and
affinity, chain-hold retry cycles, sibling-fallback circuit breaker,
mode grandfathering, and which of these reset on proxy restart (in-memory vs
persisted).

## Desired change

1. A single reference document (e.g. `proxy/docs/provider-fallback-model.md`)
   covering: chain resolution order, every knob with its layer + default +
   precedence, the failure/cooldown/quarantine taxonomies, quota/budget gating,
   mode overlays and grandfathering, and what is persisted vs in-memory.
2. `proxy/README.md` and `proxy/MODEL_ADD.md` link to it instead of duplicating
   the detail (keep short, task-focused sections there).
3. A short "inconsistencies / gaps" section recording anything found while
   writing it (knobs only available globally, provider lists duplicated in the
   fast overlay, budget gating only on one entry, etc.) — recorded as
   `discovered-from` work items rather than fixed here.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `proxy/docs/provider-fallback-model.md` exists and states, for every
   fallback-related knob: name, layer, default, precedence, and the behaviour it
   controls — verified against the code paths that read it (no invented values).
2. A precedence table covers entry > model (where applicable) > server >
   built-in default, including the mode-overlay merge rule (lists replace,
   scalars replace, dicts merge) and the `BASE_ONLY_SERVER_KEYS` inheritance
   contract.
3. The persistence section distinguishes state that survives a restart
   (`provider-state.json`, grandfathered bindings) from in-memory state
   (cooldowns, stall breaker, affinity, budget windows).
4. `proxy/README.md` and `proxy/MODEL_ADD.md` link to the new document and no
   longer contradict it.
5. Every inconsistency found is either fixed by a linked `discovered-from` item
   or explicitly recorded as accepted.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments where a pointer to the new document replaces duplicated prose.
7. Full project test suite passes (documentation-only change must not perturb
   behaviour).

## Constraints

- Documentation/analysis only: no behaviour, config-value or code-path changes in
  this item.
- Do not duplicate the new budget-gate material — reference
  `LP-0MVDQ1GMO00801PL` / `LP-0MVDUN5CY009VD20` and the per-model controls item
  (`LP-0MVDVK5TM004TQQV`) rather than restating their designs.
- UK English, Markdown, no secrets (reference API keys by env-var name only).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/docs/provider-fallback-model.md` — new reference document.
- `proxy/README.md`, `proxy/MODEL_ADD.md`, `proxy/docs/routing.md` — link + trim
  duplicated material.
- `proxy/config.yaml` — header comments point at the document.
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py`, `proxy/proxy/provider_budget.py` — verify claims;
  replace duplicated comments with pointers only where clearly redundant.

## Related work

- `LP-0MVDVK5TM004TQQV` — per-model budget knobs (the contract this document
  should describe once it lands).
- `LP-0MVDQ1GMO00801PL`, `LP-0MVDUN5CY009VD20` — the free-tier budget gate,
  reserve and wait cap.
- `LP-0MVDVJYN5001BMG4` — whether `rate_limit_rpm` should be raised.
- `LP-0MVDNP36J006430L` — header-derived budgeting.
- `LP-0MVDQKF4F008LGS6` — free tier restricted to cheap mode.

# Spike: quantify llama-server slot save/restore cost as the basis for "virtual slots"

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want measured numbers for KV-cache slot save/restore cost and
restore hit-rate, so we can decide whether "virtual slots" (e.g. 8 proxy-side session
slots multiplexed onto 2 physical GPU slots) is worth building, rather than guessing.

## Context / hypothesis to test

The proxy currently gates local dispatch with **2 dispatch leases**
(`session_slot_pool_size: 2`) and persists per-session KV snapshots
(`session_slot_save_path` / `LLAMA_SLOT_SAVE_PATH`, `_restore_slot_snapshot`,
`slot_save`). In the 24h window 2026-10-19 07:23 → 2026-10-20 07:23 there were
**2,641** `local_dispatch_denied` events (2,633 with both slots held), 5,805
contention-queue waits and 4,947 queue abandonments, while real slot occupancy was
only ≈46% once prefill (14.3 h) is added to decode (7h47m).

Hypothesis: keeping more *session* slots than *GPU* slots, and swapping a session's
KV snapshot in on demand, would let more sessions "own" local capacity without
growing the physical pool. Open question: does a restore actually avoid re-prefill
(the win), or does llama.cpp invalidate/refuse the restored cache and re-prefill
anyway (the cost)? Note: this build is Qwen3.x hybrid-attention, where llama.cpp
already invalidates its own context checkpoints, so the answer is not obvious.

## Measurements required

Using the existing harness conventions (see
`docs/slot-count-verdict-lp-0mv9ungeb009xuz5.md` for fidelity caveats):

1. **Save cost** — wall time and on-disk size of `slot save` for prompt sizes
   38K / 72K / 100K / 124K tokens; success rate (the window already shows 5
   `slot_save failed` ReadTimeouts).
2. **Restore cost + hit rate** — for a restored snapshot: `dispatch_first_byte_ms`
   vs the same session re-prefilling cold. A "hit" is a restore whose first-byte
   latency is materially below the cold prefill baseline (window baseline: median
   `dispatch_first_byte_ms` **61.8 s**, p90 **269.8 s**, max **817 s**).
3. **Invalidation behaviour** — how often the restored cache is rejected (look for
   full re-prefill / `forcing full prompt re-processing`), and the tokens re-processed.
4. **Memory/bandwidth pressure** — KV snapshot footprint per session, host page-cache
   growth for N=8 snapshots, and system MemAvailable delta.
5. **End-to-end effect under contention** — with 8 virtual slots over 2 physical
   slots and a synthetic 8-concurrent-session workload: queue abandonments,
   local serve share, and p50/p90 latency vs the N=2 baseline.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A reproducible benchmark script (committed under `proxy/benchmarks/`) that produces
   the numbers above, with fixtures/driver documented.
2. A results table in `docs/` covering save size/time, restore time, restore hit-rate,
   invalidated-restore rate, memory delta, and end-to-end contention metrics.
3. An explicit go/no-go recommendation with the break-even condition stated
   (e.g. "virtual slots pay off only if restore hit-rate ≥ X% and restore adds
   < Y s, because the cold prefill median is 61.8 s"), or a "not viable" verdict with
   the measured reason.
4. If the verdict is "not viable", name the cheaper substitutes to pursue instead
   (more physical slots — LP-0MVGCQ3QN009HRE8; idle-aware admission; shorter
   post-stream lease), with the measured evidence for each.
5. No production behaviour change is included in this item.

## Risks / notes

- Slot save/restore has failed intermittently (ReadTimeout) — the benchmark must
  record failures rather than retry them away.
- Local decode share has been hard to isolate in previous sweeps because live agent
  sessions hold the dispatch leases; the run must hold the mode lock or record the
  same validity caveat explicitly.
- Scope boundary: this spike measures feasibility and cost only; the design and
  implementation of virtual slots (if viable) is a separate follow-up item.

---

## Plan (stage `plan_complete`, 2026-10-23)

Decomposed into 7 children. Test-first tracer bullet first: the measurement
harness and its offline tests precede every measurement, so the measurement
children add columns, not plumbing. Each child is a vertical slice (code +
tests + results artifact + README/doc line), and the final child owns the
verdict document (spike AC2–AC5).

| # | Child | Type | Depends on |
|---|-------|------|------------|
| C1 | Slot save/restore measurement harness: scaffolding, fixtures, offline tests | feature | — |
| C2 | Measure slot save cost: wall time, on-disk size, success rate | task | C1 |
| C3 | Measure restore cost and restore hit-rate (cold vs restored, paired) | task | C2 |
| C4 | Characterise restored-cache invalidation (hybrid-attention behaviour) | task | C3 |
| C5 | Measure memory and page-cache pressure for N=8 session snapshots | task | C1 |
| C6 | Harness-side virtual-slot prototype: 8 session slots over 2 physical slots | task | C3, C5 |
| C7 | Results doc: tables, break-even model, go/no-go verdict and substitutes | docs | C2–C6 |

Child ids: C1 `LP-0MVKU0RG0002WWF2`, C2 `LP-0MVKU2ID0005FOJN`,
C3 `LP-0MVKU2IOR000T1OD`, C4 `LP-0MVKU2J0T0023RRW`,
C5 `LP-0MVKU49K1002FJ2X`, C6 `LP-0MVKU49VY006FVBU`,
C7 `LP-0MVKU4A7L0007KAO`.

### Parent-AC coverage

1. Reproducible benchmark script + documented fixtures/driver → C1 (harness,
   fixtures, README), numbers produced by C2–C6.
2. `docs/` results table covering all six metric groups → C7 (one AC per table).
3. Go/no-go + explicit break-even condition → C7 (break-even inequality with
   measured terms, `hit_rate*` solved per prompt size).
4. Cheaper substitutes if not viable → C7 (more physical slots / idle-aware
   admission / shorter post-stream lease, with owning ids).
5. No production behaviour change → C1 guard test, C6 constraint, C7 evidence
   section (diff restricted to `proxy/benchmarks/`, `proxy/tests/`, `docs/`).

### Seed findings from planning research (measured, not assumed)

These were established while planning and materially shape the children:

- **Restore is not exercised in production today.** Over the 35 h window
  2026-10-22 00:00 → 2026-10-23 11:00 the proxy logged `slot_save` ok 150 /
  failed 10 (6.2 %) but **zero** `slot_restore` events, and
  `scripts/analyse_slot_ratio_restore.py` reports **0** `cache_state=restored`
  dispatches. So restore hit-rate must be measured with a synthetic harness
  (`POST /slots/{id}?action=restore`), not harvested from logs — which is what
  C1/C3 do.
- **Save size is exactly measurable from llama-server's own logs.** Lines of the
  form `prompt_save: - saving prompt with length N, total state size = X MiB`
  give bytes/token directly: e.g. 57,335 tokens → 658.814 MiB (~11.8 KiB/token).
  Extrapolating, a 124 K-token snapshot is ~1.4 GiB and eight of them ~11.4 GiB
   — feasible against 41 GB `MemAvailable`, but the retention/eviction policy is
  a real cost term (C5).
- **The target sizes fit this build.** The live server runs `n_ctx_slot =
  131072` per slot at N=2, and prompts up to **124,078** tokens have been served,
  so 38 K / 72 K / 100 K / 124 K are all reachable without a config change.
- **The hit signal exists natively.** llama-server returns `timings.prompt_n`
  (tokens actually evaluated), so `cached_tokens = prompt_total − prompt_n` gives
  a token-based hit definition rather than a latency proxy; C3 makes the token
  view primary and latency corroborating.
- **Existing patterns to reuse** (do not rebuild): `scripts/ubatch_ab_benchmark.py`
  (direct llama-server HTTP, `timings`, salted prompts, percentiles),
  `proxy/benchmarks/slot_benchmark.py` (`LLAMA_PROXY_BENCHMARK_ROOT`, result
  directories, concurrency driver), `scripts/slot_persistence_harness.py` and
  `scripts/analyse_slot_ratio_restore.py` (log parsing, window metrics),
  `proxy/benchmarks/kv_memory_table.py` (per-token KV expectation),
  `scripts/cleanup-slot-cache.sh` (snapshot retention).
- **VRAM remains non-measurable.** `rocm-smi` still reports a degraded
  ~0.2 GB / 1 GB total reading on GPU[0]. C5 therefore reports VRAM as
  non-available rather than estimating it, per the convention in
  `docs/slot-count-verdict-lp-0mv9ungeb009xuz5.md`.
- **The live-run hazard is real, twice over.** Two prior live sweeps
  (LP-0MVAZPQUM006EAC7 latency caveat; LP-0MVGCQ3QN009HRE8 aborted sweep with
  600–760 s stalls and unanswered health probes) failed under concurrent agent
  load. C1's harness talks to llama-server directly, and C6 is the only child
  that needs a contention window.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

> No producer answers were received during this (unattended, herdr-downtime)
> planning run. Each question below carries the agent's recommended option and
> the plan proceeds on that recommendation; the recommendation is advisory and
> the producer may override any of them before the affected child is
> implemented. `needs-producer-review` is set for that reason.

- **Q1 — Where should the save/restore cost runs execute?**
  Options: (a) the live production llama-server on port 8080 in a quiet window
  with the mode lock held; (b) direct slot-endpoint calls against the live
  server in a low-traffic window, recording the concurrency caveat; (c) a
  dedicated, isolated llama-server on a spare port, same model and same
  `--ctx-size 262144 --parallel 2 --slot-save-path <tmp>` flags.
  **Recommended: (c)** — the measurements are pure llama-server endpoint calls
  that never need the proxy, so an isolated instance removes the live-load
  hazard that aborted the two previous sweeps; fall back to (a)/(b) only if VRAM
  cannot host the second instance.
  **Answer:** OPEN QUESTION — awaiting producer.

- **Q2 — How should measurement 5 (8 virtual slots over 2 physical slots) be
  delivered, given virtual slots do not exist and must not reach production?**
  Options: (a) a harness-side prototype under `proxy/benchmarks/` that performs
  the 8-over-2 multiplexing with real save/restore calls and measures an A/B
  against the N=2 baseline; (b) an analytic queueing model calibrated on the
  measured save/restore costs plus the historical contention logs, with no live
  A/B; (c) drop measurement 5 and reduce the spike to a cost/benefit decision
  sheet.
  **Recommended: (a)** — a spike should produce end-to-end evidence, and an
  in-harness prototype satisfies parent AC5 (no production behaviour change)
  while the eviction cost it measures is exactly the term the break-even model
  needs. Child C6 is written for (a); if the producer prefers (b) or (c), C6 is
  re-scoped or closed and C7's break-even model covers the gap.
  **Answer:** OPEN QUESTION — awaiting producer.

- **Q3 — What counts as a restore *hit*?**
  Options: (a) token-based — `cached_ratio = (prompt_total − timings.prompt_n) /
  prompt_total` with hit at ≥ 0.9; (b) latency-based — restored first-byte
  materially below the cold baseline, per the parent's AC wording; (c) both,
  reporting the token view as primary and latency as corroboration.
  **Recommended: (c)** — the token view is a direct measurement of what the
  spike is asking ("does a restore avoid re-prefill"), while the latency view is
  what the operator ultimately feels and what the parent's 61.8 s median
  baseline is expressed in; reporting both lets the verdict cite either without
  re-running. Child C3 is written for (c).
  **Answer:** OPEN QUESTION — awaiting producer.

**Research notes (no producer input required):** the seed findings above were
established by inspecting `proxy/proxy/session.py` (`_call_slot_endpoint`,
`_build_slot_context`, the circuit breaker and busy gate),
`proxy/proxy/slot_cache_ratio.py`, `proxy/config.yaml`
(`session_slot_pool_size: 2`, `session_slot_save_path`, adaptive timeout knobs),
`/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log*` and `llama-server.log*` (35 h window),
`slot-cache/` inventory, `models.ini` (`ctx-size = 262144`, `Q5_K_M`,
`slot-save-path`), and the prior verdict/reevaluation docs.
data.title: Spike: quantify llama-server slot save/restore cost for virtual slots

data.description:
## Problem statement

Four offline analysis/benchmark scripts still hard-code the **retired fast/cheap
mode-profile** routing constants (warm clamps 83285 / 100000, cheap cold 42000,
breach caps 83285 / 61440, slot pools 3 / 2). Since LP-0MVHSET0A008VU95 the live
single unified profile resolves to `warm=120000`, `cold=38000`, `slots=2`,
physical clamp `126976`, and since LP-0MVDT94F0003VHUA there is no mode axis at
all — so new `routing_check` logs (`warm_threshold=120000`) fall into no known
bucket and every per-mode cap report is meaningless.

## Users

- **Proxy operator / analyst (Richard)** — runs these scripts over proxy logs to size
  compaction, hard caps and slot geometry. Needs bucket and breach numbers that
  reflect the config actually in force, and that stay reproducible over historical
  log windows.

### Example user stories

- As an analyst, I can run `analyze_context_distribution.py` over the last 7 days and
  get session buckets and breach counts for the **current** warm cap (120000) without
  editing constants first.
- As an analyst, re-running the script over the 2026-08-24..26 window still produces
  its historical (`83285` / `100000`) buckets, so old evaluations remain reproducible.
- As an analyst, `evaluate_hard_routing_cap.py` classifies prefills against the same
  thresholds the router uses (`cold 38000`, `warm 120000`, clamp `126976`, 2 slots),
  so its "above cap" counts match live behaviour.
- As a maintainer, changing the warm cap in `proxy/config.yaml` never again requires
  an edit-and-hope sweep through analysis scripts.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **No hard-coded routing thresholds in analysis/benchmark tooling.**
   `proxy/scripts/analyze_context_distribution.py`,
   `proxy/scripts/correlate_oversized_sessions.py`,
   `proxy/scripts/run_compaction_experiment.py` and
   `proxy/benchmarks/evaluate_hard_routing_cap.py` derive their cold/warm/breach/slot
   values from `proxy/config.yaml` (or from a single shared pure resolver — see
   Constraint C2). Grep proves it: no literal `83285`, `100000`, `42000`, `61440` or
   `87381` remains as a default in those files.
2. **Current live values are produced, and historical logs still classify.**
   With the shipped config the scripts resolve `cold=38000`, `warm=120000`,
   physical clamp `126976`, `slots=2`; a `routing_check` sample carrying
   `warm_threshold=120000` lands in the current bucket (not `other`), while samples
   from older logs (`83285`, `100000`) still bucket by their **observed**
   `warm_threshold` value rather than collapsing into `other`.
3. **`evaluate_hard_routing_cap.py` MODES matches the live unified profile.**
   The fast/cheap mode split is replaced by (or collapses to) one profile with
   `cold_cache_threshold=38000`, `warm_cache_threshold_config=120000`,
   `session_slot_pool_size=2`, `local_model_ctx_size=262144`,
   `routing_clamp=126976` — or the config-derived equivalents — and
   `proxy/tests/test_evaluate_hard_routing_cap.py` (which currently asserts
   `warm_threshold(fast) == 83285` / `== 100000`) is updated to assert the derived
   values and the new prefill-bucket boundaries.
4. **Tests cover the regression.** Both test modules
   (`proxy/tests/test_analyze_context_distribution.py`,
   `proxy/tests/test_evaluate_hard_routing_cap.py`) assert against a config fixture,
   including a `warm_threshold=120000` case and a legacy `83285`/`100000` case, so a
   future cap change in `config.yaml` cannot silently desynchronise the tooling.
5. **No production behaviour change.** No file under `proxy/proxy/` changes routing
   behaviour (a pure-helper extraction, if taken, must be a behaviour-preserving move
   covered by the existing suite); docstrings/help text that describe the old mode
   profiles are corrected.
6. **Docs updated** — `proxy/docs/context-compaction-eval/README.md`,
   `docs/dev/hard-local-routing-cap-evaluation.md` and any script docstrings that
   quote the retired mode thresholds now describe the unified-profile derivation.
7. **Full project test suite passes** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **C1 — offline only.** None of these scripts is on the production routing path; a
  fix must not touch routing decisions, `provider.py` logic, or `config.yaml` values.
- **C2 — dependency weight.** The analysis scripts are deliberately stdlib-only and
  are imported directly by tests (`import analyze_context_distribution`). Importing
  `proxy.proxy.provider` would drag in `fastapi`/`httpx`; therefore prefer extracting
  the *pure* resolvers (`effective_per_slot_threshold`, warm/cold/slot/ctx getters,
  `effective_large_context_economic_ceiling`) into a stdlib-only module
  (e.g. `proxy/proxy/routing_thresholds.py`) that both `provider.py` and the scripts
  import. If the extraction proves invasive, a script-local `yaml`-based resolution
  that reuses the same formula is acceptable **provided** it is the only copy and is
  test-pinned against the live config — duplicating the formula in three scripts is
  not acceptable (it is how this defect arose).
- **C3 — historical reproducibility.** Aug-2026 evaluation artifacts
  (`proxy/docs/context-compaction-eval/distribution.{json,md}`) were produced with the
  old clamps; re-running over the same window must still yield those buckets.
- **C4 — CLI compatibility.** `--fast-cap` / `--cheap-cap` / `--mode fast|cheap` flags
  may be retired, but any removal must be documented in the docstring/help text and
  should not break the documented invocation examples.
- **C5 — repo boundaries.** No edits to `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/` in this
  item even though it carries mode-aware report logic; that skill already resolves
  per-mode triggers from config (`reporting.py:_mode_trigger`) and is not stale in the
  same way.

## Existing state

Live `proxy/config.yaml` (unified profile, mode overlays removed):

| key | value |
|---|---|
| `local_model_ctx_size` | 262144 |
| `session_slot_pool_size` | 2 |
| `local_large_context_cold_cache_threshold` | 38000 |
| `local_large_context_warm_cache_threshold` | 120000 |
| `local_large_context_economic_ceiling_ratio` | 0.4578 → ceiling 120010, capped to 120000 |
| physical per-slot clamp | `262144 // 2 - 4096` = **126976** |
| effective warm | `min(120000, 126976)` = **120000** (matches logged `warm_threshold=120000`) |

Stale constants found:

| file | symbol | value | live equivalent |
|---|---|---|---|
| `proxy/scripts/analyze_context_distribution.py` | `FAST_WARM_THRESHOLD` | 83285 | 120000 (only profile) |
| " | `CHEAP_WARM_THRESHOLD` | 100000 | — (mode retired) |
| " | `FAST_CAP` | 83285 | 120000 |
| " | `CHEAP_CAP` | 61440 | — (mode retired) |
| `proxy/scripts/correlate_oversized_sessions.py` | `FAST_CAP`, `CHEAP_CAP` | 83285, 61440 | as above |
| `proxy/scripts/run_compaction_experiment.py` | `FAST_WARM_THRESHOLD`, `CHEAP_WARM_THRESHOLD` + `Mode.from_warm_threshold` | 83285, 100000 | 120000 |
| `proxy/benchmarks/evaluate_hard_routing_cap.py` | `MODES["fast"]` | cold 38000, warm 100000, slots 3, clamp 83285 | cold 38000, warm 120000, slots 2, clamp 126976 |
| " | `MODES["cheap"]` | cold 42000, warm 100000, slots 2, clamp 100000 | (collapse to the unified profile) |

Existing single-source-of-truth helpers already in the proxy:
`provider.effective_per_slot_threshold`, `provider.effective_large_context_economic_ceiling`,
`provider.compute_hard_routing_cap` (mode argument retained but the per-mode ratios are
retired), `provider._effective_large_context_thresholds(config) -> (cold, warm)`.

## Desired change

1. Introduce one stdlib-only resolver module (or reuse an existing light one) that
   maps `config.yaml` → `(cold, warm, physical_clamp, slots, ctx_size, hard_cap)`
   using the shipped 3-term warm model, and make `provider.py` import the pure
   functions from it (behaviour-preserving move, no logic change).
2. Point all four scripts at that resolver. Replace the mode-bucket heuristic with
   **observed-value bucketing**: bucket/label each session by the `warm_threshold`
   value in its own log lines (e.g. `warm=120000`, `warm=83285`), and compute breach
   counts against the resolved cap for the *current* config by default, with a
   `--warm-cap`/`--cold-cap` override for historical replay. `warm_threshold=120000`
   must therefore be a first-class bucket, and the `other` fallback only catches
   genuinely unknown values.
3. Collapse `evaluate_hard_routing_cap.MODES` to a single profile derived from config;
   keep the `--mode` flag only if it remains meaningful (otherwise retire it and say so
   in the docstring). Update the two test modules accordingly.
4. Correct every docstring/help string that still describes the fast/cheap mode
   profiles as live.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/proxy/routing_thresholds.py` — New (or equivalent): stdlib-only pure resolvers for effective cold/warm/clamp/slots from a config dict, extracted from `provider.py`.
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — Import the pure resolvers from the new module (behaviour-preserving; no logic change).
- `proxy/scripts/analyze_context_distribution.py` — Drop the four hard-coded constants; resolve thresholds from config; replace mode bucketing with observed-`warm_threshold` bucketing; correct the docstring's "Mode classification" section.
- `proxy/scripts/correlate_oversized_sessions.py` — Drop its duplicated `FAST_CAP`/`CHEAP_CAP`; use the shared resolver and the same bucket keys as the analyser.
- `proxy/scripts/run_compaction_experiment.py` — Drop `FAST_WARM_THRESHOLD`/`CHEAP_WARM_THRESHOLD` and the `Mode.from_warm_threshold` table.
- `proxy/benchmarks/evaluate_hard_routing_cap.py` — Replace `MODES` fast/cheap entries with the single config-derived profile (`cold 38000`, `warm 120000`, slots 2, clamp 126976).
- `proxy/tests/test_analyze_context_distribution.py` — Assert config-derived thresholds plus a `warm_threshold=120000` case and legacy 83285/100000 cases.
- `proxy/tests/test_evaluate_hard_routing_cap.py` — Replace the pinned `83285`/`100000` assertions with derived values and new bucket boundaries.
- `proxy/tests/test_routing_thresholds.py` — New: pin the extracted resolver against the shipped `config.yaml` values (cold 38000, warm 120000, clamp 126976).
- `proxy/docs/context-compaction-eval/README.md` — Update the script description and invocation examples (no `--fast-cap`/`--cheap-cap` mode wording).
- `docs/dev/hard-local-routing-cap-evaluation.md` — Update the mode-constant description to the unified profile.

## Related work

- LP-0MVHSET0A008VU95 — Raise local warm-context routing cap 100K → 120K (and the economic-ceiling ratio that binds it). *Origin of the drift; completed.*
- LP-0MVDT94F0003VHUA — Priority-based routing replacing fast/cheap mode (epic, completed). *Retired the mode axis these scripts still model.*
- LP-0MTVXP7DG00613ZB — Unified `compaction_trigger_ratio` / retirement of `local_hard_routing_cap_ratio_fast`.
- LP-0MU466L1X003RTHN — 3-term warm model (`min(physical clamp, economic ceiling)`); the formula the resolver must reuse.
- LP-0MSAZXXDY005AWA1 — Physical per-slot clamp (`ctx_size // slots - 4096`).
- LP-0MTC87GBV0031F4B — F1 session context-size distribution analysis (author of `analyze_context_distribution.py`).
- LP-0MTAQNAIH001RN1S — Hard local-routing cap evaluation (author of `evaluate_hard_routing_cap.py`).
- LP-0MTBOX45O005LD1S — Implement hard local-routing cap (fast 70K / cheap 61.4K) + cheap compaction gate. *Origin of the `61440` cheap cap these scripts still quote.*
- LP-0MTLB1LK80098R43 — Revert hard-routing cap to dynamic (disable 70K/61.4K caps). *Superseded the absolute caps; the analysis scripts never followed.*
- LP-0MVNCMDW50043RSP — Geometry A/B protocol and reporter (open): also manipulates `session_slot_pool_size` and warm/cold thresholds; will want the same resolver.
- LP-0MVMHNUXW0061FGN — Experiment: 1 slot at 262K ctx vs 2 slots at 131K ctx (open): its arm geometry will invalidate any hard-coded constants again — reinforces deriving from config.

## Risks & assumptions

- **R1 — silent formula duplication.** Fixing the numbers by editing literals satisfies AC2 but recreates the defect at the next cap change. *Mitigation:* AC1's grep check + AC4's config-fixture tests.
- **R2 — provider refactor risk.** Extracting resolvers out of `provider.py` touches production code for a tooling defect. *Mitigation:* pure move only, no logic change, full suite gate; fall back to a script-local `yaml` resolver (C2) if the move destabilises `provider.py`.
- **R3 — historical comparability.** Observed-value bucketing changes bucket *labels* (`fast`/`cheap` → `warm=<n>`), so old and new artifacts are not byte-comparable. *Mitigation:* documented in the script docstring and README; the `--warm-cap`/`--cold-cap` overrides preserve old numbers on demand.
- **R4 — scope creep.** Other stale mode references certainly exist elsewhere (e.g. `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/` report text, docs prose beyond the two files above). *Mitigation:* C5 keeps the skill out of scope; file follow-ups as `discovered-from` items rather than expanding this low-priority chore.
- **A1 (assumption).** The fast/cheap mode axis is genuinely retired, so collapsing to a single unified profile is correct; the mode labels are not to be preserved as a *config* concept. Evidence: `proxy/proxy/config_merge.py` ("mode overlays … were removed"), `provider.py` (`compute_hard_routing_cap` uses the unified profile unconditionally), `config.yaml` (only `local_hard_routing_cap_ratio_fast` marked RETIRED, single slot pool/slot thresholds).
- **A2 (assumption).** `correlate_oversized_sessions.py` and `run_compaction_experiment.py` are in scope even though the seed text named only two scripts: they carry the same constants and one imports the analyser's helpers, so fixing only the named two would leave the same defect one file away. Recorded here rather than as a blocker.
- **A3 (assumption).** `PyYAML` may be used by the scripts if the pure-helper extraction is rejected, because `proxy/requirements.txt` pins `pyyaml>=6.0` and the scripts run in the proxy venv.
- **A4 (assumption).** No operator-facing behaviour depends on the scripts' `--mode`/`--fast-cap` flag names; retiring them is acceptable with documented help text.
- **No production backlog impact:** priority `low` (analysis tooling only, no live behaviour affected) is retained.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

The seed description supplied a concrete problem statement, two named files and
three acceptance criteria; repo search answered every remaining question, so no
operator interview was required.

- Q: Which config values are live today? — Answer (repo): `session_slot_pool_size: 2`,
  `local_model_ctx_size: 262144`, cold 38000, warm 120000, ratio 0.4578 → effective
  warm `min(120000, 262144//2-4096=126976) = 120000`. Source: `proxy/config.yaml`
  (lines ~1261, ~1296, ~1395, ~1649), `proxy/proxy/provider.py`
  `_effective_large_context_thresholds`.
- Q: Is the fast/cheap mode axis dead, i.e. should the fix collapse to one profile? —
  Answer: yes (assumption A1). Source: `proxy/proxy/config_merge.py` header
  ("mode overlays … were removed"), LP-0MVDT94F0003VHUA (completed epic).
- Q: Are there more stale copies than the two named scripts? — Answer: yes, two more —
  `correlate_oversized_sessions.py` (`FAST_CAP`/`CHEAP_CAP`) and
  `run_compaction_experiment.py` (`FAST_WARM_THRESHOLD`/`CHEAP_WARM_THRESHOLD` +
  `Mode.from_warm_threshold`). Source: `grep -rn '83285\|100000\|61440' proxy/scripts
  proxy/benchmarks`. Added to scope under assumption A2.
- Q: Can the scripts import the proxy's resolver directly? — Answer: not cleanly —
  `provider.py` imports `httpx`/`fastapi` while the analysis scripts are stdlib-only
  and are imported bare by tests. Hence constraint C2 (extract pure helpers, or a
  single script-local resolver) and risk R2.
- Q: Must historical eval windows still reproduce? — Answer: yes (constraint C3), so
  bucket by the observed `warm_threshold` value rather than only by the current config
  (assumption/R3, AC2).


## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MTLB1LK80098R43** – Revert hard-routing cap to dynamic (disable 70K/61.4K caps) — follow-up to LP-0MTBTCK2I005MOTE verdict (completed)
- **LP-0MTVPJBF0001SQF4** – Cap empty-response cooldown at 10s instead of exponential backoff (completed)

# Goal (bug)

As an operator, I want a change to `models.ini` or `start-llama.sh` (model launch arguments: `ubatch-size`, `batch-size`, `ctx-size`, cache types, …) to force a llama-server restart on `start-proxy.sh --restart`, so a config edit is never silently left inactive.

## Evidence (2026-10-22, LP-0MVIQ0FSX006HQOS)

Setting `ubatch-size = 2048` in `models.ini` [Qwen3] and `UBATCH_SIZE=2048` / `LLAMA_UBATCH_SIZE:=2048` in `start-llama.sh`, then running `scripts/start-proxy.sh --restart`, left llama-server running with `--ubatch-size 1024`. Cause: the preserve decision hashes only the merged `config.yaml`

```
_restart_sha=$(merged_config_sha256(config.yaml, <overlay>))
# compared with .llama_server_signature.json config_sha256
if [ "$_sig_sha" = "$_restart_sha" ]; then KEEP_LLAMA=1; fi
```

`models.ini` and `start-llama.sh` are the actual launch-argument sources (the startup log even prints `BATCH_SIZE=…`), but they are not part of the signature, so any edit to them is invisible to the restart decision.

Workaround used at the time: delete `proxy/.llama_server_signature.json` to force `KEEP_LLAMA=0`. That is undocumented and easy to get wrong (the file lives under `proxy/`, not the repo root, although the script computes `REPO_ROOT` as the parent of `proxy/`).

## Proposed change

1. Include the model-launch inputs in the restart signature: hash `models.ini` and `start-llama.sh` (and any other launch-argument source the launch path reads, e.g. the ini selected by `$LLAMA_MODELS_PRESET` when set) alongside the merged config.
2. Surface the reason in the restart output, e.g. `Restarting llama-server: models.ini changed since last start`, next to the existing preserve message.
3. Document the forced-restart escape hatch (removing `proxy/.llama_server_signature.json`, and a `--force-llama-server` flag if one is added) in the start-proxy skill and `proxy/README.md`.
4. Fail-safe direction: a signature file written before this change carries no launch-input hashes, so the first `--restart` after upgrading sees a mismatch and restarts llama-server once — same fail-safe precedent as LP-0MUJRVYQH002IEHW (a wrong preserve is worse than one cold start).
5. One shared helper: the signature is **written** by `proxy/proxy/lifecycle.py` (`_write_llama_server_signature` → `_config_file_sha256`) and **read** by both `proxy/scripts/start-proxy.sh` (restart gate) and `lifecycle._try_adopt_running_llama_server` (adoption gate). All three must derive the same extended value, so the extension belongs in the shared `proxy/proxy/config_merge.py` helper surface, not duplicated in shell.

## Key Files

- `proxy/scripts/start-proxy.sh` — restart gate (`KEEP_LLAMA` decision, `_sig_sha` vs `_restart_sha`), `--keep-llama-server` flag parsing; signature file resolved as `$REPO_ROOT/.llama_server_signature.json` where `REPO_ROOT` is `proxy/`.
- `proxy/proxy/lifecycle.py` — write path `_config_file_sha256()` / `_write_llama_server_signature()` (~lines 65–115); adoption gate `_try_adopt_running_llama_server()` (LP-0MUPIIDPW009RMLB, ~line 145); `_llama_server_signature_path()`.
- `proxy/proxy/config_merge.py` — home of the shared `merged_config_sha256()` helper; extend/add the launch-input signature helper here so shell and Python agree byte-for-byte, with a JSON/CLI entry point the shell can call.
- `start-llama.sh` — launch-argument source: reads `models.ini` (`ngl`, per-model `ctx-size`), builds `--batch-size` / `--ubatch-size` / `--ctx-size` / cache flags; prints `BATCH_SIZE=…` at startup.
- `models.ini` — per-model and `[global]` launch arguments (`ngl`, `ctx-size`, `ubatch-size`, …).
- `tests/test_start_proxy_mode.sh` — bash harness with stubbed `pkill` and existing unchanged / base-only / overlay-only restart tests; natural home for the models.ini and start-llama.sh restart tests.
- `proxy/tests/test_restart_lifecycle.py` — signature write/read and adoption hash-mismatch tests.
- `proxy/tests/test_config_merge.py` — shared-hash helper tests.
- `proxy/README.md` — restart-signature section (~line 1290) and `start-proxy.sh` CLI flags table (~line 1855).
- `.pi/skills/start-proxy/SKILL.md` — operator-facing restart guidance. AC5 explicitly authorises this edit; it is agent-framework infrastructure and out of bounds under normal repository boundaries.

## Implementation notes (test-first)

1. **Tests first.** Extend `tests/test_start_proxy_mode.sh` with: a `models.ini` value change restarts, a `models.ini` comment-only change restarts, a `start-llama.sh` change restarts, and an unchanged trio still preserves. Extend `proxy/tests/test_restart_lifecycle.py` and `proxy/tests/test_config_merge.py` with writer-side parity and adoption rejection on a launch-input change.
2. **Shared helper.** Add the extended signature (signature value + per-input hashes) to `proxy/proxy/config_merge.py`, callable both from Python and from the shell gate, so `start-proxy.sh` never reimplements hashing.
3. **Signature payload.** Persist per-input hashes in `proxy/.llama_server_signature.json` (e.g. `launch_inputs: {"models.ini": "<sha>", "start-llama.sh": "<sha>"}`) so the gate can name exactly what changed; keep the existing `config_sha256`/`model`/`parallel`/`router_mode` keys.
4. **Shell gate.** Compute the extended signature in the `--restart` block and, on mismatch, echo e.g. `Restarting llama-server: models.ini changed since last start` (falling back to a generic message when the change cannot be attributed).
5. **Docs.** `proxy/README.md` restart-signature section + CLI flags table, and `.pi/skills/start-proxy/SKILL.md`.

## Verification

- Targeted: `bash tests/test_start_proxy_mode.sh` and `python3 -m pytest proxy/tests/test_restart_lifecycle.py proxy/tests/test_config_merge.py` (single-file/targeted runs are permitted; the full suite goes through `/skill:test`).
- Manual (AC1): edit `models.ini`, run `proxy/scripts/start-proxy.sh --restart`, confirm the restart output names the changed input and the new process argv / `BATCH_SIZE=` line reflects the edit.
- Full suite green via `/skill:test` before commit.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: Editing `models.ini` (a comment-only change and a value change, tested separately) followed by `start-proxy.sh --restart` restarts llama-server (test or documented manual verification with the observed argv).
- AC2: Editing `start-llama.sh` likewise restarts llama-server.
- AC3: An unchanged config/models.ini/start-llama.sh trio still preserves the warm llama-server (no regression to LP-0MUCEFCL6001ZXYN).
- AC4: The restart output captured in the startup log names which launch input changed, e.g. `Restarting llama-server: models.ini changed since last start`.
- AC5: The forced-restart path is documented in `.pi/skills/start-proxy/SKILL.md` and `proxy/README.md` (minimum: removing `proxy/.llama_server_signature.json`; documenting a `--force-llama-server` flag instead is acceptable if one is added).
- AC6: The Python write path (`lifecycle._config_file_sha256` / signature writer) and the adoption gate (`_try_adopt_running_llama_server`) derive the same extended signature as the shell restart gate — one shared helper, parity covered by a test — so an unchanged trio is still preserved on every path and an edited launch input is rejected on every path.
- AC7: Full test suite green; commit + hash recorded.

## Assumptions / out of scope

- Launch inputs are hashed as raw file bytes, so a comment-only `models.ini` edit also forces a restart (AC1 requires this explicitly).
- In-scope launch inputs are the resolved models ini (repo-root `models.ini`, or the ini named by `$LLAMA_MODELS_PRESET` when set) and the resolved launch script (repo-root `start-llama.sh`, or `server.llama_start_script` when configured). The container launch path (`scripts/podman_start_llama.sh`) does not read `models.ini` and is out of scope.
- No child decomposition: the effort/risk estimate is Small effort (~12 h recommended, range 9.8–16.5 h) and Medium risk — one vertical slice (shared helper + shell gate + Python writer + tests + docs), so child items would add ceremony without independent deliverables.

## Related work

- LP-0MVIQ0FSX006HQOS — the ubatch A/B where this was hit (reverted; commit c9a49039).
- LP-0MUCEFCL6001ZXYN — the original "preserve the warm llama-server on a proxy-only restart" decision this must not regress.
- LP-0MVAPNC2900145RH — restart-reason plumbing in the same script.
- LP-0MUJRVYQH002IEHW — merged-config (base + overlay) signature; the precedent this change extends.
- LP-0MUPIIDPW009RMLB — the same signature hash on the hot-swap adoption path.

# Instrument and fix the slot sidecar seed path (restored-prefix warmness never fires)

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want the restored-prefix credit (LP-0MVGD9YXH008O304) to
actually fire for sessions that resume with a persisted slot snapshot, so the
feature is measurable — and if it cannot fire for the common case, I want to
know why with instrumentation instead of silence.

## Problem statement

The ≥24 h measurement (LP-0MVGGPSVM003W35K, 2026-10-22) found the seeding path
made **zero contact** in a 54.4 h post-deploy window:

- 0 `slot_ratio_restored` events, 0 `cache_state=restored` lines;
- the sidecar writer is healthy: 37 `slot_<session>.bin.ratio.json` sidecars
  written (2026-10-20 13:27 → 2026-10-22 19:43), names match the reader's
  candidate layout (`slot-cache/localhost-8080/`);
- 33 sessions with sidecars reached the local routing gate 2,918 times after
  their sidecar existed (including right after proxy restarts when the in-memory
  ratio was empty) and were still scored `cache_state=cold` — e.g. session
  `herdr-1792667491-…` (sidecar: 276 messages, saved 14:13) scored
  `cached_ratio=0.00 cache_state=cold messages=696` at 19:30 after a restart.

Root-cause suspects (in order of likelihood): (1) the `prefix_matches` guard
fails on real resumed conversations — first message (system prompt) regenerated
per request, and/or client-side compaction rewriting the front of the history
(proxy-side compaction is disabled: `compaction_bypass_eval … reason=compaction_disabled`);
(2) sidecars only exist for old snapshots, so a 24 h TTL plus front-rewrites
leaves no credit window; (3) (checked, unlikely) endpoint string drift between
save and seed. Seed outcomes log at DEBUG only, invisible at the INFO level the
proxy runs at.

## Split at producer request (2026-10-22)

The producer chose **instrument first**. The observability half is now its own S
child, **LP-0MVJYZWWW005XGW7** (INFO-level `slot_ratio_seed outcome=…` logging +
tests + docs), and this item depends on it. Do not change the credit logic
(`prefix_matches`, the sidecar TTL, the sidecar format) until the interface has
produced one traffic cycle of outcome counts: a fix attempted without that data
is guesswork. Effort below (M) covers the remaining fix plus the ≥24 h
re-measurement; priority is medium while it waits on data.

## Proposed change

1. Using the instrumented outcome counts, decide which failure mode is real:
   too-strict `prefix_matches` (rewritten system prompt / client-compacted
   history), an expired sidecar (24 h TTL vs long-lived sessions), or a lookup
   miss. Record the decision and the supporting data on this item.
2. Fix only the confirmed cause, consistent with AC2 of LP-0MVGD9YXH008O304 (a
   *changed* prompt still earns nothing; a *reusable prefix* must earn credit).
   Candidate approaches to evaluate: fingerprint the non-system messages only;
   anchor on a stable prompt-prefix hash; credit the last-saved overlapping
   messages; or compare against the last K messages of the stored list instead
   of requiring a prefix. Re-evaluate the TTL if it is the binding constraint.
3. Add a unit test reproducing the real resume pattern (sidecar saved for a full
   conversation; resumed request arrives with a rebuilt system prompt or a
   compacted front) that fails before the fix and passes after it.
4. Re-run the ≥24 h before/after measurement with
   `scripts/analyse_slot_ratio_restore.py` (built by LP-0MVGGPSVM003W35K):
   post-fix `cache_state=restored` dispatches must be > 0, and seeded dispatches
   must beat cold dispatches in the same context bucket (sample counts +
   percentiles).
5. Document the changed guard in `proxy/docs/routing.md`.

## Acceptance criteria

- A written verdict on this item names the confirmed failure mode and cites the instrumented outcome counts that prove it.
- For the confirmed cause, a unit test reproduces the resume-with-rewritten-front case and fails on the pre-fix code.
- After the fix, a ≥24 h window contains `cache_state=restored` dispatches, and their `dispatch_to_first_byte_ms` percentiles are stated against cold dispatches in the same context bucket with sample counts.
- No regression on AC2/AC3 of LP-0MVGD9YXH008O304 (mismatched snapshots earn nothing; restored ratio ≤ measured × margin).
- `proxy/docs/routing.md` documents the resolved guard and its failure modes.

## Risks / notes

- The 24 h TTL (`session_slot_ratio_ttl_seconds`) may itself be too short for
  the resume pattern observed (sidecar at 276 messages, resume at 696); include
  TTL in the investigation.
- Attribution caveat: the local-prefill improvement in the measurement window
  came from other changes (expected-reuse credit, admission ordering); do not
  use it as evidence for this path.

## Traceability

- discovered-from: LP-0MVGGPSVM003W35K (the AC5 measurement that found zero seeds)
- implementation of: LP-0MVGD9YXH008O304 (restored slot-prefix warmness)
- blocked by: LP-0MVJYZWWW005XGW7 (seed-outcome instrumentation)
- report: docs/dev/slot-prefix-warmness-measurement-LP-0MVGGPSVM003W35K.md

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/proxy/slot_cache_ratio.py` — the seed path and its guard: `prefix_matches()`,
  `seed_cached_ratio()` (validation order: snapshot → sidecar → model → TTL → prefix),
  `ttl_seconds()` / `_is_expired()`. The confirmed-cause fix lands here.
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — `expected_cached_ratio()` applies the *same*
  `prefix_matches` guard to the in-memory expected-reuse credit (~L812); a guard change
  must be evaluated for both call sites, not just the sidecar.
- `proxy/tests/test_slot_cache_ratio_restore.py` — add the resume-with-rewritten-front
  reproducer alongside the existing guard/TTL tests.
- `proxy/docs/routing.md` — restored-prefix warmness section (~L475–530): document the
  resolved guard and its failure modes.
- `scripts/analyse_slot_ratio_restore.py` — the AC3 re-measurement.
- `docs/dev/slot-prefix-warmness-measurement-LP-0MVGGPSVM003W35K.md` — the baseline the
  re-measurement is compared against.

## Plan (features and implementation tasks, 2026-10-22)

The five acceptance criteria decompose into three independently deliverable
slices plus the prerequisite instrumentation, in dependency order (verification
slices before implementation, per the plan skill's test-first rule):

| # | Work item | Type | Covers | Depends on |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **LP-0MVJYZWWW005XGW7** — Instrument slot-sidecar seed outcomes at INFO | task (S, risk Low) | prerequisite data (INFO `slot_ratio_seed outcome=…`) | — |
| 1 | **LP-0MVK0E8C40035FG3** — Diagnose the seed failure mode from outcome counts | task (verification) | AC1 | item 0 |
| 2 | **LP-0MVK0E80C009HUQC** — Fix the confirmed seed guard and document it | bug (test-first slice) | AC2, AC4, AC5 | item 1 |
| 3 | **LP-0MVK0E8NH007XCV3** — Re-measure restored vs cold over ≥24 h after the fix | task (verification) | AC3 | item 2 |

**Why three slices:** AC1 needs the instrumentation's outcome counts (a
traffic-cycle wait), and AC3 needs a ≥24 h post-fix window (another wait).
Neither wait can complete inside a single fix run, so each is its own item
with its own worktree lifecycle; the fix itself stays one vertical slice
(code + failing-then-passing test + docs) rather than being split
horizontally.

**Deliberately undecided:** the fix technique (non-system fingerprinting, a
stable prompt-prefix anchor, last-K overlap credit, or a TTL change) is chosen
from the diagnosis verdict, not here — the producer's "instrument first" split
stands. A fix attempted without the outcome counts is guesswork.

**Between phases:** after the diagnosis verdict lands, re-read the fix item's
description and update it so the reproducer test and the guard change match
the confirmed mode; after the fix lands, confirm the deployed build before the
re-measurement window starts.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MVJYZWWW005XGW7** – Instrument slot-sidecar seed outcomes at INFO (measure before fixing) (open)
- **LP-0MVGGPSVM003W35K** – Measure restored slot-prefix warmness impact over >=24h (before/after) (completed)
- **LP-0MVI2XOTY008Q4UV** – Second-turn cached_ratio scored 0.00 after a successful cold first local turn (bootstrap defect in update_cached_ratio) (completed)

### Repository file matches (verified by inspection)
- `proxy/proxy/slot_cache_ratio.py` — `prefix_matches()` (the suspected guard), `seed_cached_ratio()` validation order, `ttl_seconds()` / `_is_expired()` (TTL), `_candidate_slot_filenames()` (lookup)
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — `expected_cached_ratio()` reuses the same `prefix_matches` guard for the in-memory expected-reuse credit (~L812), so any guard change affects both paths; `_last_prompt_prefix` store
- `proxy/tests/test_slot_cache_ratio_restore.py` — existing guard/TTL tests (`test_changed_system_prompt_does_not_match`, `test_front_truncated_history_does_not_match`, `test_expired_sidecar_earns_no_credit`, `test_ttl_zero_disables_expiry`) to extend with the resume-with-rewritten-front case
- `proxy/docs/routing.md` — restored-prefix warmness section (~L475–530) to update
- `scripts/analyse_slot_ratio_restore.py` — ≥24 h before/after re-measurement tool
- `docs/dev/slot-prefix-warmness-measurement-LP-0MVGGPSVM003W35K.md` — baseline figures and sidecar inventory to compare against

## Intake notes (verification pass, 2026-10-22)

- **No interview required.** The seed brief already carried a problem statement with
  evidence, five measurable acceptance criteria, scoped constraints ("do not change the
  credit logic until the instrumentation has produced one traffic cycle"), risks and
  traceability; the remaining questions are answerable from the repo, which was read
  during this pass (seed path, guard, tests, docs, measurement report).
- **Duplicate check performed** (`wl search` on "slot sidecar restored prefix warmness"):
  no duplicate item exists. Related, non-overlapping items are the completed implementation
  LP-0MVGD9YXH008O304, the completed measurement LP-0MVGGPSVM003W35K (which triggered this
  item), the open instrumentation child LP-0MVJYZWWW005XGW7 and the completed
  expected-reuse credit LP-0MVI2XOTY008Q4UV.
- **Assumption (recorded, not decided):** the failure mode is not chosen here. The
  producer's "instrument first" split stands — this item stays `blocked` on
  LP-0MVJYZWWW005XGW7 and its fix is selected from the instrumented outcome counts.
- **Note on the shared guard:** because `prefix_matches` is also used by
  `provider.expected_cached_ratio()` for the in-memory expected-reuse credit, any guard
  change is a two-call-site change; the AC2 unit test must therefore assert the sidecar
  path *and* confirm the expected-reuse path still refuses a genuinely changed prompt
  (AC4).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers (plan, 2026-10-22)

**No operator questions were asked in this session.** Rationale: the intake
brief already carried the producer's "instrument first" decision, five
measurable ACs, explicit scope constraints and full traceability; the
plan-approval gate returned `request_approval: false` (effort Medium, risk
Medium — the gate pauses only for Extra Large effort combined with High/Severe
risk), so no approval pause was warranted. Everything the plan needed was
answerable from this work item and the repository, which was read during this
session.

**Decision log (agent-made, evidence-linked):**

- **D1 — decompose into three children** instead of implementing as one unit.
  Evidence: AC1 depends on a traffic cycle of instrumentation data and AC3 on
  a ≥24 h post-fix window; both are waits that cannot complete inside a fix
  run. Splitting lets each be worked, reviewed and closed on its own worktree
  lifecycle.
- **D2 — keep the reproducer test inside the fix item** (TDD slice), not in a
  separate child. Evidence: AC2 requires the test to fail on the *pre-fix*
  code, so a standalone red test cannot be delivered or closed independently;
  width comes from tests-plus-docs inside the slice instead.
- **D3 — converted the numbered AC lists to bullet form** (this item and its
  instrumentation child), text unchanged. Evidence: the shared tree-coverage
  review (`shared/tree_coverage.extract_acceptance_criteria`) reads `- `
  bullets only, so numbered ACs made the automated parent↔child coverage check
  report vacuously "fully covered". No requirement text was altered.
- **D4 — the fix technique stays open** until the diagnosis verdict names the
  failure mode; recorded on the fix item (its step 2) and on this item's
  "Proposed change" section.
- **D5 — the 24 h TTL is in scope only if the diagnosis proves it binding**;
  the fix item must then record the observed `age_s` distribution as the
  numerical justification.
- **D6 — instrumentation child advanced to `plan_complete`** via the plan
  skill's auto-complete path (effort S, risk Low): its existing ACs, proposed
  change and risks were reviewed, and a verified `## Key Files` section was
  added from this session's repository reads.

**Assumptions (recorded, not decided):** the instrumentation build reaches
production and serves one full traffic cycle; the confirmed cause stays inside
the documented seed path (guard, TTL, lookup); the guard change must be applied
at both `prefix_matches` call sites (sidecar seed and in-memory expected-reuse
credit).

**OPEN QUESTION:** none blocking. The one open *technical* question — which
guard semantics are correct — is intentionally deferred to the diagnosis
verdict (item LP-0MVK0E8C40035FG3) and is not an operator decision.

## Plan: changelog (2026-10-22)

- **2026-10-22T20:41Z** — planned child LP-0MVJYZWWW005XGW7 (effort S, risk
  Low → auto-plan skip path): reviewed its requirements/AC alignment,
  completeness, sequencing, scope, testability and polish; added a verified
  `## Key Files` section; converted its AC list to bullets; stage advanced to
  `plan_complete`.
- **2026-10-22T20:45Z** — created children LP-0MVK0E8C40035FG3 (diagnosis),
  LP-0MVK0E80C009HUQC (fix + reproducer test + docs),
  LP-0MVK0E8NH007XCV3 (≥24 h re-measurement); wired the dependency chain
  instrumentation → diagnosis → fix → re-measurement.
- **2026-10-22T20:47Z** — added this Plan section and Appendix; converted this
  item's AC list to bullets (text unchanged) so the shared tree-coverage review
  can verify the child↔AC mapping.

## Validation reports

- `docs/dev/slot-ratio-restore-postfix-2026-10-30.md` — post-deploy
  verification of the restored-prefix seed fix (`5502ee44`), with JSON
  artifacts `docs/dev/slot-ratio-restore-postfix-2026-10-30.json`,
  `docs/dev/slot-ratio-restore-postfix-2026-10-30-full.json` and
  `docs/dev/slot-ratio-restore-postfix-2026-10-31.json`.
  Produced by LP-0MVTJVNSO008IZEB; answers **AC3 of this epic**.
  **Verdict: NOT FIXED** — 0 `cache_state=restored` dispatches, 0
  `slot_ratio_restored` seed events and 0 `slot_ratio_seed outcome=found`
  over a 39.17 h post-fix window (895 seed decisions), with
  `missing_sidecar` at 96.4 %. Root cause work continues in
  LP-0MVVI8TEU006KTOZ (writer-side sidecar still absent at seed time).

## Problem statement

Six `REFACTOR-<work-item-id>` provenance markers are still embedded in `proxy/` sources even though every referenced work item is **completed**. The refactor skill injects these markers when it files a smell (`remediate_pre_existing()` → `inject_refactor_comment()`) but nothing removes them when the item closes, so stale markers re-trigger refactor scans and re-file duplicate work items (LP-0MVIR51KL0096QOB was re-filed against an already-fixed F823 smell that LP-0MVJXC9MK003UET8 had resolved).

## Users

- **Maintainer running a refactor scan** — story: "As a maintainer, I want refactor scans to only report smells that still exist, so I do not triage duplicate work items."
- **Reviewer reading source** — story: "As a reviewer, I want the REFACTOR comments I see in source to point at open work, so provenance comments do not become permanent noise."

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every `REFACTOR-<id>` marker in `proxy/` whose work item is `completed`/`closed` is removed, together with any now-empty leading comment line — audited by a scripted check that greps `REFACTOR-` across the repo and asserts each remaining marker references a non-terminal work item.
